References: Viewfinder and Superliminal (the first-person view, clean readable spaces, and surprise from space that does not behave).
View: 3D · Camera: first person at eye height, mouse look, smoothed.
Two lives of one place, colourful and red, with different walls and doors
Arches you see through and walk through with no cut
A room bigger inside than outside
A path round a corner that leads somewhere new the second time
A door that leads to a different place from each side
Cubes you carry through arches onto switches that open doors
Five spaces, one idea each: shown safe, then used, then twisted
A clear sound and the gate lighting the moment a space is solved
teleport like a portal between the lifes · in the slice
a bit more non-ecludiean ideas · in the slice
simple puzzles · in the slice *(guessed)*
You stand on a garden path facing a glowing arch, with red ground showing through it.
You walk through and you are in the red life with no cut; looking back, the green garden is inside the arch.
A wall blocks the path in red but not in green, so you cross back at a second arch and pass it.
Then a tiny shed with one door: you step in and it is a long hall, far bigger than the shed.
The exit gate at its end lights when you reach it.
*(provisional)* The first real puzzle is the third space, around minute three.
A switch in the colourful life needs a cube that exists only in the red life, and the hedge path round a pillar leads somewhere new the second time round, so the short way is not the way.
Nothing kills you and nothing is lost: R restarts the space, and a cube that falls out of reach returns to its start.
Spaces four and five combine the bigger-inside room, the changing path, and a door that leads to a different place from each side.
